ANALYSIS: Acropustulosis of infancy is a recurrent sterile vesiculopustular eruption localized to the hands/feet of infants; dyshidrotic eczema (pompholyx) is a vesicular eczematous dermatitis typically seen in older children/adults with different triggers and chronicity. They are distinct entities.

VERDICT: INCORRECT

ANALYSIS: Adams–Oliver syndrome is a multisystem genetic disorder classically featuring aplasia cutis congenita of the scalp plus limb and sometimes cardiovascular/neurologic anomalies. Labeling the finding as isolated aplasia cutis congenita omits the syndromic diagnosis and associated systemic features, so they are not equivalent.

VERDICT: INCORRECT
